Form ADV Part 2A × 13F

What they say, against what they hold

get_institution_profile

The Part 2A brochure is the only place a manager describes, in its own words, how it invests. A 13F says nothing about intent, only exposure. Read together they can disagree — a firm can describe a blend mandate and run a book whose multiples read as growth.

Form ADV Part 2A · Item 5

What the funds charge

get_institution_profile

The fee schedule as the brochure prints it. The parsed rate is for scanning; where it and the sentence disagree, the sentence wins.

Replicating portfolio

Trading only on what had been filed

get_market_dataget_benchmark_prices

Each book is bought at the close of the first trading day after its 13F appeared on EDGAR and held until the next filing — buying at quarter-end would use information nobody had yet. Long US-listed equity only: no shorts, options or non-US listings, so this is not the fund's own performance.

    Risk-adjusted

    How much of the return is just beta

    Beta against the index, and annualised Jensen alpha (risk-free at zero). Upper right is money made picking stocks; lower right is a rise bought with market exposure.

    Attribution

    What carried the book, and what cost it

    Each name's contribution to the replicating portfolio — weight times its move while held, summed across holding periods.

    Per filing

    Excess return, holding period by holding period

    One cell per filed book, from the day it was bought to the day it was replaced, against the index over the same days. A consistent sign says more than any one big period.

      Build your own, on your own data

      This page is a frozen snapshot. Its source is public on GitHub. Paste the prompt below into Claude: it fetches that source and republishes it reading live FocusAlpha data through your connector — your universe, your filters, your account.

      1. Connect FocusAlpha in your preferred AI, if you haven’t already Connect →
      2. Copy the prompt below and paste it into a new conversation
      3. Edit the conditions at the bottom — that last block is yours to change
      4. Claude fetches the page's source from GitHub, publishes it with your connector, and applies your conditions
      Build me a live fund dashboard from the FocusAlpha sample at https://app.focusalpha.ai/manager-profile-dashboard, on a manager I follow.

The page is open source. Fetch this ONE file and use it verbatim as the page:
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/focusAlpha/dashboards/main/manager-profile-dashboard/live.html
It is a single self-contained HTML file, about 115 KB, no build step, no dependencies. Download it
exactly as it is, with curl or your fetch tool. Do not summarise it, retype it, or rebuild it from
memory. The sample on focusalpha.ai is this same page with Lone Pine's data frozen on 2026-09-23
baked in; live.html reads everything through the FocusAlpha connector: the Form ADV profile and
brochure, the filed 13F book quarter by quarter, prices for the replication, and the ^SP500TR
benchmark.

Then, in this order:
1. Publish the file as an artifact, declaring the connector:
     capabilities: { mcp: { servers: [{ server: "FocusAlpha", tools: ["search_institutions", "search_companies", "get_institution_profile", "get_institutional_holdings", "get_market_data", "get_benchmark_prices"] }] } }
   If the connector is listed in your tools as "focusalpha", use that spelling for server.
   Without this declaration window.claude.use('mcp') resolves null and the page can never fetch.
2. Open it and check that it loads Lone Pine live; the status line counts the calls it made. If the
   page says the connector is not available, I have to connect FocusAlpha first:
   https://focusalpha.ai/start
3. Now change the fund. The PEERS list near the top of the script holds the default fund (the first
   entry) and its peers, each with a CIK and a CRD. Call search_institutions({ q: "<name>",
   has_style: true }) for my fund and for each peer I name, put my fund first, republish, and send
   me the link. The page's own search box can load any fund at runtime; the list only sets the
   default and the peer set.

Rules for any change:
- Keep the data layer exactly as it is: every read goes through the page's call() helper into
  MCP.callTool. Never paste rows into the page. The point of this page is that it fetches its own data.
- A 13F is not AUM. It is long US-listed equity only: no shorts, no options, no non-US listings.
  A falling line can be a drawdown or a move into assets the form does not cover, and the filing
  cannot tell those apart. The page says so; keep it.
- The replication buys each book at the close of the FIRST TRADING DAY AFTER its 13F appeared,
  never at quarter end, because the quarter-end price uses information nobody had yet. Keep it,
  and keep it labelled as a replication, not as the fund's return.
